adversary_objection: The proposal can fail because intranasal administration simply does not deliver a biologically meaningful amount of intact, membrane-protected EVs to the sampled CNS compartments at the chosen short post-dose interval (or the delivered intact-EV fraction is below orthogonal assay sensitivity), so there will be no reproducible linkage between verified in vivo intact-EV exposure and any ex vivo microglial single-cell transcriptional signature. This is supported by direct non-human-primate biodistribution data showing negligible brain/CSF recovery and strong nasal retention after intranasal EV dosing (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution); even if rodent efficacy papers report functional outcomes after intranasal EVs (ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi), those do not establish orthogonally verified intact-EV exposure and may reflect formulation-, species-, or secretome-dependent effects. Compounding this, MISEV2023 warns that EV separation/characterization and membrane-protection assays are technically challenging and that spike-in or capture reagents may not faithfully report in vivo EV behavior (ev-misev2023-quality-framework). Together, these imply a bounded failure mode where either (a) real intact-EV exposure is absent in vivo, or (b) intact-EV exposure is present but below detection/verification limits or not faithfully reported by the spike-in/capture assays, producing no reliable correlation with the single-cell readout.
assumptions: Assay sensitivity: immuno-capture and particle-count instrumentation are sufficiently sensitive to detect orthogonal intact-EV signatures in short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue samples.
Spike-in validity: an exogenous, orthogonally labeled intact-EV spike-in is available and behaves as an internal recovery control without altering biological readouts.
Feasibility: short-interval tissue harvest and single-cell processing are operationally feasible within the chosen animal model and institutional/ethical approvals.
biological_rationale: Rodent intranasal studies report functional effects but lack orthogonal intact-EV exposure linkage (ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi). MISEV2023 emphasizes membrane-protection and orthogonal controls to attribute activity to intact EVs (ev-misev2023-quality-framework). A spike-in–controlled in vivo→ex vivo bridge with a single-cell transcriptional readout in tissue-resident microglia provides a higher-dimensional, mechanism-relevant discrimination between membrane-protected EV-associated effects and soluble/secretome artifacts; this addresses translation risk flagged by macaque biodistribution uncertainty (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution).

edges.competing_explanation: Observed ex vivo transcriptional changes could be driven by soluble secretome components that reach sampled compartments independently of intact EVs.
edges.missing_experiment: Spike-in–controlled in vivo→ex vivo bridge with membrane-disruption and capture-depleted arms combined with single-cell transcriptomics.
edges.model_or_species: rodent context for ex vivo readout
edges.uncertainty: High: rodent efficacy literature shows functional outcomes but lacks orthogonal intact-EV exposure linkage; inference required to propose single-cell microglial readout as a discriminating PD endpoint.

edges.competing_explanation: Failure to detect intact-EV exposure in larger species may reflect administration route, labeling sensitivity, or species-specific clearance rather than absence of EV-mediated exposure.
edges.missing_experiment: Matched intact-EV verification assay in short-interval in vivo samples concurrent with ex vivo single-cell readout.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: macaque data demonstrate intranasal delivery limitations that heighten the need for orthogonal in vivo verification; competing explanations include formulation/administration differences or labeling artifacts.

nodes.statement: An orthogonally defined intact-EV signature (exogenous spike-in recovery + capture-positive signal that co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive) identifies a membrane-protected particle fraction in the administered material.

If orthogonally verified intact-EV exposure is present in short-interval nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa samples after intranasal dosing, then ex vivo tissue-resident microglia isolated from treated animals will show a reproducible, specific single-cell transcriptional modulation (distinct cluster-level gene-expression shifts) relative to controls.

If the administered material is capture-depleted or membrane-disrupted prior to dosing, or lacks the spike-in–validated intact-EV signature, then the short-interval ex vivo microglial transcriptional modulation will be absent or qualitatively different, indicating the effect depends on intact EV-associated cargo rather than particle abundance or soluble secretome.

chair_rationale: The hypothesis is scientifically plausible but unsupported by key empirical data and requires targeted de-risking before adoption. Critical evidence gaps include: (1) in vivo validation that the exogenous spike-in faithfully models endogenous EV biodistribution and membrane-protection in the intended species/matrices; (2) demonstration that immuno-capture + particle-count orthogonal assays have sufficient sensitivity/specificity in short-interval nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-adjacent tissue; and (3) timing/kinetic data showing intact-EV presence in sampled compartments. Substantial CMC/scale-up and stability risks (reproducible production of capture-positive vs capture-depleted fractions, lot comparability) further necessitate process studies. Recommend spike-in behavior validation, orthogonal assay sensitivity experiments in the target species/matrices, and small-scale manufacturing comparability/stability studies prior to progressing to in vivo efficacy/potency testing.
competing_explanations: Soluble secretome components that co-fractionate or survive membrane disruption mediate ex vivo transcriptional changes independent of intact EVs.
Apparent orthogonal in vivo exposure may reflect residual label or spike-in/tracer artifacts rather than native intact-EV delivery.
dependencies: Access to a characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer and validated immuno-capture reagents
Short-interval in vivo sampling approvals and operational setup
design_question: Daily question: Does orthogonally verified in vivo exposure of a spike-in–validated, membrane-protected intact-EV fraction after intranasal dosing causally produce a reproducible short-interval ex vivo microglial transcriptional signature that is lost when the same material is membrane-disrupted or capture-depleted?
expected_measurable_effect: If the hypothesis is supported: short-interval (predefined brief post-dose window) ex vivo single-cell RNA-seq of microglia-like cells from olfactory-bulb–adjacent tissue will show a reproducible transcriptional signature (cluster shift and differential expression of predefined inflammatory/regenerative gene modules) that correlates with orthogonal in vivo evidence of intact-EV exposure (presence of capture-positive spike-in-validated signal and particle co-localization). This signature will be absent or qualitatively altered in capture-depleted or detergent/protease-treated arms (falsification outcome).
explicit_inferences: Inference: Rodent intranasal efficacy signals motivate an in vivo→ex vivo bridge but do not establish intact-EV exposure; orthogonal spike-in and membrane-protection controls are required to attribute ex vivo transcriptional modulation to intact EVs (labeling and assay controls per MISEV2023).

Inference: A single-cell transcriptional readout in tissue-resident microglia increases mechanistic resolution relative to bulk cytokine assays and can discriminate subtle, EV-dependent PD signals from soluble-secretome effects.
falsification_criteria: Validated spike-in recovery in capture-positive fractions is observed but no reproducible microglial single-cell transcriptional signature is detected across independent biological replicates (n >= 3), implying intact-EV exposure does not produce the proposed short-interval ex vivo effect.

Particle-count–matched capture-depleted or detergent/protease-disrupted arms produce equivalent microglial transcriptional responses to capture-positive arms, indicating the effect is not dependent on intact EV capture/protection.
human_decisions_required: Select single-cell microglial transcriptional modules / gene sets to predefine as the primary mechanistic readout
Approve source-cell lot and production parity for the bounded vs secretome preparations
Approve animal numbers, short-interval timing, and ethical protocols
manufacturability_assessment: Requires production of matched bounded (capture-positive) and secretome-retaining preparations from the same source-cell lot, plus a characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in. Early investment in orthogonal capture reagents, particle counting, and single-cell processing capacity is needed; success would focus CMC on fractionation and process envelopes that preserve membrane protection.
manufacturing_rationale: Requiring a spike-in–validated, membrane-protected fraction as the drug-substance identity gate focuses CMC development on fractionation and process conditions that preserve membrane integrity (reducing downstream assay ambiguity), enabling targeted potency assay development and comparability testing per MISEV guidance.
measurement_strategy: Qualitative orthogonal in vivo verification (spike-in recovery + capture-positive particle co-localization + detergent/protease sensitivity) plus ex vivo single-cell RNA-seq of microglia with predefined module-based readout (presence/absence and reproducibility across replicates). Use spike-in to control assay recovery and include detergent/protease and capture-depleted arms to falsify EV-dependence.

minimum_discriminating_experiment.assay: Integrated orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo workflow: (A) pre-dose in vitro characterization of all arms with density/size fractionation, particle counts per fraction, immuno-capture readouts for endogenous markers and spike-in tracer, and detergent/protease protection testing; (B) intranasal administration (randomized animals) with a predefined short post-dose interval optimized to maximize recoverable signal; (C) collect nasal lavage, CSF (if feasible), and olfactory-bulb–adjacent tissue; (D) orthogonally verify intact-EV exposure in collected fluids/tissue (capture + particle counts + spike-in recovery); (E) isolate tissue microglia (acutely) and perform single-cell RNA-seq; (F) analyze for predefined transcriptional modules (inflammatory and regenerative gene sets) and cluster shifts comparing arms; (G) correlate presence/absence and reproducibility of microglial single-cell signature with orthogonal in vivo exposure evidence.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.comparator: Four-arm in vivo design (same conditioned-medium lot; all arms spiked identically with exogenous tracer prior to fractionation where applicable): (1) intact-EV–enriched preparation (capture-positive bounded fraction), (2) secretome-retaining concentrated conditioned medium, (3) intact-EV–enriched preparation treated with detergent + protease (membrane-disrupted) prior to administration, (4) particle-count–matched but capture-depleted preparation (if achievable).
minimum_discriminating_experiment.control: Positive assay controls: characterized small EVs and dexamethasone in ex vivo microglial assay; negative controls: vehicle-only and buffer fractions; internal recovery control: exogenous spike-in per sample; capture-compatibility and spike-in controls to exclude assay interference.
dependencies: Availability of an orthogonally labeled intact-EV spike-in tracer and validated capture reagents
Operational single-cell RNA-seq capacity and bioinformatics pipeline for microglial module analysis
Animal protocol approvals for short-interval tissue/fluid collection
minimum_discriminating_experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible linkage between orthogonal in vivo intact-EV verification and the ex vivo microglial single-cell signature across replicates (i.e., capture-positive verification does not predict the transcriptional outcome), or particle-count–matched capture-negative or membrane-disrupted arms produce equivalent single-cell signatures, indicating the effect is not intact-EV–dependent.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.falsification_outcome: If failure criteria are met (with validated spike-in recovery and capture-compatibility controls), the hypothesis is falsified: short-interval microglial transcriptional modulation is not dependent on intact-EV exposure for this preparation and route. The program must treat the material as functionally indistinguishable from secretome for short-interval PD and redirect potency/CMC strategy accordingly.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.hypothesis_tested: An orthogonally verified, membrane-protected intact-EV fraction (spike-in validated, capture-positive, particle-peak co-localized, detergent/protease-sensitive) is necessary for a reproducible short-interval ex vivo microglial transcriptional modulation following intranasal dosing; particle-count-matched capture-depleted or membrane-disrupted material will not produce the same transcriptional signature.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative, reproducible presence (yes/no across replicates) of a predefined microglial single-cell transcriptional signature (cluster-level differential expression of inflammatory/regenerative modules) in animals dosed with capture-positive, spike-in–validated intact-EV material that correlates with orthogonal evidence of intact-EV exposure (capture-positive signal co-localized with particle peaks and spike-in recovery) and is absent or qualitatively altered in membrane-disrupted or capture-depleted arms.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.question: Does orthogonally verified intact-EV exposure (spike-in recovery + capture-positive particle co-localization + detergent/protease sensitivity) after intranasal dosing produce a reproducible short-interval ex vivo microglial single-cell transcriptional modulation that is lost when the same material is membrane-disrupted or capture-depleted?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium from a single characterized source-cell lot processed into: (A) bounded intact-EV–enriched fraction (e.g., program-defined SEC/iodixanol-bounded) and (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) from same lot
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled) to add pre-fractionation for recovery controls
Immuno-capture reagents for canonical EV surface markers (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5) and validated capture-compatibility buffers
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent), protease (proteinase K), and RNase reagents for membrane-disruption/protection controls
Density-gradient materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors

Animal model: rodents suitable for short-interval intranasal dosing and rapid tissue harvest (approved protocol), with capacity for collecting nasal lavage, CSF (if feasible), and olfactory-bulb–adjacent tissue
Single-cell RNA-seq pipeline reagents and instrumentation for microglia isolation (enzymatic tissue dissociation, microglia enrichment), library prep, sequencing, and downstream analysis pipelines
Controls: characterized small-EV positive control material; vehicle-only and buffer-only negative controls; dexamethasone or known anti-inflammatory control for assay validation
secondary_readouts: Spike-in tracer recovery percentage and membrane-protection behavior in lavage/CSF/tissue capture fractions (qualitative: recovered & detergent-sensitive vs not recovered)
Co-localization metrics between particle-count peaks and capture-positive ELISA signal in both administered material and recovered lavage/CSF fractions
Protein:particle ratios of administered materials and of captured fractions

Single-cell metrics: proportion of microglia in altered transcriptional clusters, differential expression of predefined gene modules, and reproducibility across biological replicates (n >= 3 animals per arm, multiple independent conditioned-medium preps if feasible)
minimum_discriminating_experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: across independent replicates (n >= 3 animals per arm and >= 3 conditioned-medium preps where feasible), only animals dosed with spike-in–validated, capture-positive intact-EV material reproducibly show the predefined microglial single-cell transcriptional signature; this signature is abolished or absent in membrane-disrupted or capture-depleted arms, and orthogonal in vivo exposure metrics (spike-in recovery + capture co-localized with particle peaks) are concordant with the presence/absence of the signature.

novelty_statement: Novelty: This hypothesis couples per-sample exogenous intact-EV spike-in recovery and orthogonal capture/protection verification in short-interval in vivo samples with an ex vivo single-cell transcriptional readout of tissue-resident microglia. Prior SGL-001 proposals used bulk cytokine or ELISA-based ex vivo readouts; the proposed single-cell microglial transcriptomic bridge provides a higher-resolution, mechanism-relevant PD discriminator that is not present in the cited prior hypotheses and is designed specifically to discriminate intact-EV–associated potency from soluble secretome effects under matched orthogonal exposure controls.
principal_risks: Assay sensitivity: inability to detect orthogonal intact-EV exposure in short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue confounds interpretation.
Spike-in behavior: spike-in tracer may not faithfully reflect endogenous EV behavior in vivo.
Biological relevance: microglial transcriptional changes may be subtle or confounded by tissue harvest stress.
proposed_potency_relationship: If present reproducibly, the single-cell microglial transcriptional signature will serve as a qualitative potency gate predictive of short-interval PD linked to intact-EV exposure; absence across replicates falsifies EV-mediated short-interval PD for this assay.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt a mechanism-linked potency gate defined as: a spike-in–validated, membrane-protected intact-EV fraction (capture-positive, particle-peak co-localized, detergent/protease-sensitive) that predicts a reproducible short-interval ex vivo microglial transcriptional modulation after intranasal administration; use as a qualitative potency-linked product-identity attribute (non-numeric).

concerns: Key inference-labeling and attribution are appropriate, but the central causal inference is speculative: canonical rodent efficacy studies (ev-zhuang-2011, ev-kodali-2017, ev-hermann-2023) document functional outcomes without orthogonal intact-EV exposure verification, so using them to infer intact-EV–dependent microglial single-cell PD is indirect and high-uncertainty (proposal acknowledges this).

Spike-in validity is assumed but unsupported by the supplied evidence: no canonical data show an exogenous labeled EV spike-in reliably mirrors endogenous EV biodistribution, recovery, or membrane-protection behavior in vivo (explicit evidence gap).

Assay sensitivity / detection limits: MISEV2023 (ev-misev2023) recommends orthogonal characterization, but it does not guarantee that immuno-capture + particle counters can detect intact-EV signatures in short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue in the chosen model; NHP data (ev-driedonks-2022) demonstrate intranasal signal can be negligible and retained in nasal lavage, raising realistic risk of non-detectability or false negatives.

Translational generalizability: ev-driedonks-2022 reports negligible brain uptake after intranasal EVs in macaques; the proposal flags this as a competing explanation but additional evidence is needed to support generalization from rodent single-cell readouts to larger species or humans.

Potential for label/tracer artifacts: the plan must guard against residual label or spike-in tracer artifacts producing apparent orthogonal exposure—this competing explanation is noted in the proposal but not resolved by the canonical evidence.

Reliance on a qualitative (presence/absence) potency gate increases interpretive risk versus a quantitative, reproducible metric; MISEV2023 supports orthogonal controls but does not validate the proposed qualitative single-cell gate as a regulatory-ready potency assay.
reviewer_findings.conclusion: Not supported as a validated claim. The proposal is a coherent, methodologically reasonable experimental plan grounded in MISEV2023 best-practices and in rodent intranasal efficacy reports, and it correctly cites NHP biodistribution limitations as a translational risk. However, the central causal claim—that orthogonally verified, spike-in–validated intact-EV exposure after intranasal dosing produces a reproducible short-interval ex vivo microglial single-cell transcriptional signature that is lost with membrane disruption or capture-depletion—lacks direct empirical support in the supplied canonical evidence and therefore remains unproven and high-risk until the proposed experiments are executed.
reviewer_findings.evidence_gap: No supplied canonical evidence demonstrates (a) that an exogenous intact-EV spike-in behaves as a faithful in vivo recovery/internal control for endogenous EVs after intranasal administration, or (b) that orthogonally verified in vivo intact-EV exposure (spike-in recovery + capture-positive, detergent-sensitive signal) causally correlates with a reproducible short-interval single-cell microglial transcriptional signature. Rodent efficacy studies report functional effects but explicitly lack orthogonal intact-EV exposure linkage; macaque data show intranasal delivery limitations, underscoring translational uncertainty. These specific linkages and spike-in validation experiments are missing.

concerns: Manufacturability and process sensitivity: Producing matched bounded (capture-positive) and capture-depleted or membrane-disrupted fractions reproducibly from a clinical-scale source-cell lot is high-risk. Process windows that preserve membrane integrity during concentration, fractionation (SEC/iodixanol), and storage are narrow and not demonstrated in cited materials (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Measurement feasibility and assay sensitivity: The strategy depends on orthogonal spike-in recovery and immuno-capture co-localized with particle peaks in short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue. MISEV emphasizes orthogonal controls (ev-misev2023-quality-framework), but the macaque data show intranasal EVs may be below detection in CSF/brain and retained in nasal lavage (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution), raising real risk that assay sensitivity or route/formulation—not biology—will drive negative results.

Spike-in validity: The plan assumes an exogenous orthogonally labeled intact-EV spike-in will mimic endogenous EV pharmacokinetics and membrane-protection in vivo. This behavior is unproven; if the spike-in behaves differently, it will confound recovery-based gating and potency attribution (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Lot comparability and stability: Defining product identity as a qualitative, spike-in–validated membrane-protected fraction shifts CMC toward tight control of fractionation and storage. There is no evidence here that protein:particle ratios, membrane integrity measures, or capture-positivity are stable across lots or during scaled processing and storage; stability-indicating assays and comparability protocols must be developed (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Scale-up risk: Fractionation methods (SEC, density gradients) that are feasible at small scale for exploratory animals may not translate to clinical-scale manufacturing without introducing shear, dilution, or reagent impurities that disrupt membrane protection and capture-positivity; this is a significant development risk (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Translational risk from species differences: Rodent intranasal efficacy and PD signals motivate the experiment (ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi), but macaque biodistribution shows limited intranasal brain access (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution). Failure to detect intact-EV exposure in larger species could reflect route/formulation/species differences rather than assay limits, complicating interpretation and regulatory justification for the proposed potency gate.

Quality-attribute relevance: The proposed qualitative potency gate (presence/absence of a microglial single-cell signature linked to orthogonal intact-EV exposure) is exploratory and not yet tied to a quantifiable, stability-indicating CQA or to clinically relevant endpoints; regulators will expect robust assay validation, stability linkage, and comparability before accepting it as a product-identity attribute (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).
reviewer_findings.conclusion: Not supported as a robust, near-term CMC/potency strategy without additional de-risking. The proposal is scientifically plausible for exploratory rodent studies and aligns with MISEV2023 recommendations for orthogonal characterization (ev-misev2023-quality-framework) and with rodent intranasal efficacy reports that motivate an exposure→PD bridge (ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi). However, key manufacturability, scale-up, measurement-sensitivity, stability, and lot-comparability risks remain unresolved and are amplified by non-human-primate intranasal biodistribution data showing poor recoverable intact-EV signal and strong nasal retention (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution). Without targeted de-risking experiments (validated spike-in behavior in vivo, orthogonal capture sensitivity in target species, and process-capable fractionation preserving membrane integrity at scale), this attribute cannot be relied on as a product-identity/potency gate for development.
reviewer_findings.evidence_gap: Critical gaps: (1) empirical demonstration that the proposed orthogonal spike-in and capture assays have sufficient sensitivity and specificity in the intended in vivo species and matrices (nasal lavage, CSF, olfactory-adjacent tissue); (2) validation that the exogenous spike-in faithfully models endogenous product EV behavior (recovery, retention, membrane-protection) in vivo; (3) process studies showing reproducible production of bounded (capture-positive) versus capture-depleted preparations from the same source-cell lot with acceptable lot-to-lot comparability and stability under relevant storage/handling; (4) scale-up feasibility data demonstrating fractionation and membrane-protection preservation at production scales.

concerns: Assay sensitivity and recovery: Short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue sampling may yield EV concentrations near or below detection limits; negative exposure readouts could reflect assay insensitivity rather than true absence of intact EVs (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution; ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Spike-in validity: Exogenous tracer behavior may not faithfully model endogenous EV pharmacokinetics or membrane stability in vivo; differential trafficking or clearance of the spike-in could confound recovery-based inference (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Species and route generalizability: Positive rodent intranasal outcomes do not guarantee intact-EV delivery in larger species or humans; macaque data show strong nasal retention and negligible brain uptake for certain EV preparations, so a rodent-positive result may not predict translational delivery (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution; ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome).

Specificity of microglial transcriptional readout: Microglial single-cell signatures can be affected by tissue harvest, anesthesia, or systemic inflammatory signals; predefined, validated modules and appropriate non-EV controls (vehicle, soluble secretome, detergent/protease) are required to avoid misattribution (ev-misev2023-quality-framework; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi).

Feasibility of capture-depleted and particle-matched arms: Generating particle-count–matched but capture-depleted material without altering other bioactive components is technically challenging; incomplete depletion or co-removal of soluble factors could muddy comparisons (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Timing and kinetics: The optimal short post-dose window for detecting intact-EV exposure and consequent microglial transcriptional changes is uncertain; poorly chosen intervals risk false negatives or capturing secondary, non–EV-mediated effects (ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi).

Interpretation if orthogonal metrics disagree: Scenarios where spike-in recovery is low but a microglial signature is observed (or vice versa) will be difficult to interpret without additional controls (e.g., labeled endogenous-EV tracers, longitudinal sampling) (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Statistical reproducibility and sample size: The proposal's success criterion requires reproducibility across animals and conditioned-medium preps; small n or batch variability could produce misleading conclusions—predefinition of n and independent preps is essential (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).
reviewer_findings.conclusion: The proposed in vivo→ex vivo bridge is conceptually plausible and well-aligned with MISEV2023 recommendations: orthogonal, membrane-protection controls plus an exogenous spike-in and single-cell microglial readout could, in principle, distinguish intact-EV–dependent short-interval PD from soluble-secretome effects in rodents. Prior rodent intranasal reports of functional outcomes (ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi) make the mechanistic question relevant, while MISEV2023 (ev-misev2023-quality-framework) explicitly supports the need for orthogonal capture/protection assays and appropriate controls. However, there is high uncertainty in translating intranasal intact-EV exposure across species and formulations (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution), and several technical and interpretive risks must be mitigated before a causal attribution to intact EVs can be claimed. If implemented with the proposed orthogonal controls, detergent/protease arms, and validated spike-in recovery, the experiment is capable of discriminating the key competing explanations (intact-EV–mediated vs secretome-mediated effects), but success depends critically on assay sensitivity, spike-in validity, timing/sample recovery, and predefined microglial module selection.

title: Hypothesis: A spike-in–validated, membrane-protected intact-EV fraction predicts a reproducible short-interval ex vivo microglial transcriptional modulation after intranasal dosing (single-cell readout)
